text: You also learn well inside a frame like a school or a discipline, and you keep studying long after the course has ended.
issue: "Even so" concedes against a line that is not there. On D059, D085 and D198 the line before it makes no contrary claim, and on D059 it says the same thing ("you learn easily inside a course or a school").

text: So far your closest friendships have been between equals, people who did not need you to rescue them. You gave less time to the friends who wanted looking after, and you kept the level ones.
issue: Day lived beats also run as "the pattern so far" for readers under 35, before the Home Chapter has begun.

text: Winter's last month is the coldest stretch of your year, and your Wood sits frozen with no sign of growth. The season asks for Metal first to split you open and then for Fire to catch in the opened grain, the one it cannot do without. You shine in the deep cold the moment that flame takes hold.
issue: "The half" makes the reader parse the sentence twice.

text: You grew in those years by going your own way, away from what was expected of you. The progress was real and nearly invisible, and you kept going on your own conviction while you felt behind.
issue: Banned hedge.

text: In your first home someone gave you books, questions or long silences in place of the usual fuss, an adult who lived in their own head. By your teens you had learned to answer your own questions, and you asked for help less than other children did.
issue: Banned hedge.

text: You end up in charge in most places you work, before you have asked for it. Because pressure has been familiar since your first years, you take on serious work that makes others nervous. You rise through hard roles, and you find easy ones dull within months.
issue: Banned hedge.

text: Money comes to you through openings in these years more than through regular pay, an offer or a sale or a well-timed move. You take more chances with money in this decade than you are used to, and most of them pay.
issue: Banned word.

text: Openings came your way in those years, a timely move or a chance offer or someone who knew someone. Money reached you by routes regular pay never took, and you grew bolder with it.
issue: Banned word.

text: What you have earned since your late teens has followed your instinct, with good runs and lean months in turn. At least once you have lost the gains of a good year by chasing a better one, and you have learned how your own streaks run.
issue: Banned word.

text: You earn in bursts, a run of good months and a quiet stretch after. Because each good season makes you sure of the next, you spend the winnings on a new chance before you have kept any. You are richer in the middle of each good stretch than after it.
issue: Banned word.

text: Your chances with money grow the further you go.
issue: Banned word in a headline.

text: You spend quickly and generously, and money that comes in through friends or windfalls goes out the same way. Because a free hand with money was admired at home when you were young, saving feels cautious to you in a way you dislike. Your bank balance swings more than most people's, and you are calm about it until a lean month arrives.
issue: Banned word.

text: Careful earning paid off in those years, and you saved steadily from regular work. You built up something solid without windfalls or risk, and you trusted your own counting more than any tip.
issue: Banned word.

text: In family life you expect warmth, and you give it back without thinking. Because care at home was steady from the start, you trust your relatives easily and find it hard to believe the worst of them. You take it harder than most when a relative lets you down, because you never expected it.
issue: Pain word.

text: The Magistrate sits beside your General, and you switch between fighting for ground and asking for it politely. People above you get mixed signals, and you lose credit that one clear approach would win.
issue: On B002 and B028 the Magistrate sits inside a branch (丑, 申), not on show.

text: Your chart is without the General, and nobody inside it sets you a hard test or a date you cannot move. You keep your own pace and face few real trials, and you learn how strong you are only when pressure comes from outside.
issue: "test" appears twice in the unit.

text: Your chart gives the Steward no place, and nobody inside it keeps the books or counts what comes in. You handle money in bursts and forget it for months, and you rely on a partner or a spreadsheet to keep track.
issue: "count" twice.

text: The Alchemist your season asks for lies as a thin thread far beneath the surface, and you reach for strange knowledge only when ordinary answers run out.
issue: "run" twice in one sentence.

text: The Artisan your season asks for stays beneath the surface, and you refill yourself through a private craft or a slow meal at home.
issue: It asserts the reader lives alone.

text: A quiet friction runs between a partner and the people after you, and you spend years smoothing over complaints nobody says out loud.
issue: "Your partner" assumes the reader has one. The law, and every other bond unit, says "a partner".

text: The household you grew up in gives your working life a running start, and you walk through doors your parents or siblings opened for you.
issue: The idiom is broken: one walks through a door, one does not build on it.

text: Freezing rain frosts you over in midwinter and hides the sun. The month's first need is Water in full flow to keep you clean and moving, and its second the sun's Fire, with Earth and Wood steadying both. You glitter in the cold once those two are close beside you.
issue: "Its" has no clear antecedent: it could be the freezing rain or midwinter.

text: You have almost nowhere to stand in midsummer, a thin rain falling into the fiercest heat of the year. The season asks for Metal of both kinds to give you a source, and for more Water beside you to guard that Metal from the heat. You get through this season once others like you stand with you.
issue: The close asserts peers on every 五月癸 chart, but B054 holds no Twin and no Rival, and its own MISSING lines say so.

text: A hard deadline settles you instead of rattling you, and you turn out your best work when the clock runs short.
issue: On every page where this pairing fires, the General's seen line already says "when the stakes are high".

text: Your chart answers to pressure, the hard test and the person who pushes back. You rise when the risk is real and the deadline is close, and you are steadiest in the thick of a fight.
issue: On every 七杀格 page with a General on show, it sits beside "the person people send in when the stakes are high".

text: Every part of your life adds to one story, from your first home through work and partnership to the people after you, and you watch it gather weight.
issue: The Hour Gate's locked phrase is "the people after you".

text: Your chart buries the Magistrate your season asks for in a deep corner, and you take on a formal role late and grow into it slowly.
issue: The stem can sit in more than one branch, so "one" is false on B094.

text: The Metal season peaks in the middle of autumn, and it takes more out of your ground than any other month. Water returns first as rain to refill you and Fire follows to warm your strength back, with fine Metal feeding the rain, and you hold firm against the season with all three at your side.
issue: The sentence names three elements and then says "both".

text: Plans and people far from home pulled you away in those years, and your family saw less of you than they wanted. You made it up in bursts of generosity, and you came through because your family forgave more than you expected.
issue: "Came through on" is a broken idiom.

text: Your family has scattered across more than one place since your late forties, and the younger ones live far from you and from each other. You have become the one who brings them together, and your best days in these years have been reunions.
issue: "Those years" puts in the past the gate the reader is still living in (48 on, now).

text: You keep your household running, the cupboards full and the bills paid before they are due. Because a well-kept home is how you show love, you feel uneasy when things at home are left undone. Your family feels safe without knowing how much you do, and you rarely tell them.
issue: A compound adjective before its noun takes a hyphen (the corpus already writes "strong-willed" and "mid-thirties").

text: Your family life has been built on structure, with regular meals, shared duties and arrangements that hold. Relatives on both sides have come to trust your household, and you have been the one who kept its promises when others forgot.
issue: The list misparses on first read, and "keeps" clashes in tense with "forgot".

text: Keeping the household in order weighs on you in these years, and you carry more of it than your share. The routines you built keep you going, and you pass some of the load over once your family sees it.
issue: "Order" comes twice in two short sentences.

text: Your family sheltered you in those years more than you needed, and the care came with expectations. You kept the peace by doing as you were asked, and what carried you was one thing you chose for yourself.
issue: "Expectations" and "expected" clash across two adjacent sentences.

text: The expectations you grew up with stay with you, and you feel uneasy when a family duty goes undone. Because approval at home came through doing things right, you check yourself against what your elders would think. Your bond with your family is strong and dutiful, and you feel its pull wherever you live.
issue: It asserts the reader has left home, which the chart cannot know (D130 is 26). The Year seat reads the family of origin (渊海子平 年为祖上), not where the reader lives.

text: Caution about money tightens in these years, and spending on yourself feels wrong even when you can afford it. You have more put by than you feel you have, and you relax a little each time you check.
issue: "should" is banned on these pages.

text: Chances to earn keep reaching you from your late forties, through younger people or through a move. Your money stays lively in these years, and you sleep best when one part of it is never touched.
issue: "move" and "moves" in one unit, in two senses.

text: Younger people start to make claims on your money from your late forties. You will give more than you planned each time, and you will keep your own share only where you set its size before anyone asks.
issue: "Keep your own floor" is not a B1 idiom, and "the number" needs a second read.

text: You treat money in a relationship as joint, and you give freely when a partner wants something. Because loyalty to the person beside you outweighs any careful plan, the shared accounts blur and the arguments arrive later. You stay calmest about money when your share and theirs are kept apart, and you seldom manage it.
issue: "Your partner" asserts that the reader has one now, where Q10 allows "a partner".

text: You love by doing, the meal made and the evening kept free and the worry taken off someone's hands. Since giving comfort is how you feel close, you feel most loved by a partner who receives it gladly and gives some back. You give without keeping count, and you are the last of your friends to notice a partner who only takes.
issue: "Much later" can attach to "takes", so the close has to be read twice.

text: In love you fall for the one with plans and friends and somewhere to be. Because range is what draws you, you lose interest within months in a partner who only offers closeness. What you want is someone who brings the world home, and you grow restless with anyone who shuts it out.
issue: The recognition opens on the headline word for word.

text: Love settles from your mid-thirties into a partnership between two people who each run their own lives. Over these years the score between you matters less, and you lean on a partner without feeling smaller.
issue: A tally does not grow shorter, and "you can lean" is a capacity close.

text: The people you have loved were strong-willed and hard to predict, and they made you earn every point you won. At least one relationship of yours ran loud for years, with fights over plans and whose turn it was, and you stayed because it held your interest.
issue: "stayed" twice in one sentence.

text: You show love by talking and teasing, and a quiet partner leaves you lonely even in a happy home. Since you feel close only when your mind is met, you keep testing a partner with argument, and some evenings end colder than either of you meant. What you want is praise and honesty in the same person, and you rarely settle for half.
issue: "Your partner" asserts that the reader has one now, where Q10 allows "a partner".

text: You climb at work through trust, the clean record and the job done the proper way. Because being correct matters to you, you follow the rules others bend, and senior people notice. You rise steadily, and you find it hard to take a risk that could mark your record.
issue: "should" is banned on these pages.

text: You give freely in your family, the treat paid for and the loan made without terms. Because an older relative showed you that generosity makes people love you, you find it hard to refuse anyone close. You keep giving past what you can afford, and you resent it only later.
issue: It says the opposite of what it means ("after you can no longer afford to").

text: You work best on things that feed people in some way, a meal or a lesson or a well-made thing. Because making something well gives you more pleasure than any title, you turn down promotions that would take you away from the work itself. Your work runs on appetite, and you do more of it in a happy month than in a pressured year.
issue: "pleasure" twice in one unit.

text: Comfort dulled your drive at work in those years, and easy work held you longer than it served you. You were well liked and under-stretched, and the skill you practised for pleasure is what kept you going.
issue: "should" is banned, and "kept" prints twice in one sentence.

text: You are trusted at work because you know your subject properly, and people check their facts with you. Because depth matters more to you than visibility, you leave the self-promotion to others, and promotion reaches you later than your knowledge has earned it. Your standing grows slowly and holds when louder careers fall away.
issue: "should" is banned.

text: Good food and long evenings cost you energy in these years, and the easy option wins more days than you mean it to. You hold steady through a simple routine you enjoy, and you keep to it because it gives you pleasure.
issue: "should" is banned.

text: Pressure costs you sleep and energy through these years, and short nights add up faster than you notice. What carries you is rest and slow meals given their place in the week, and you recover fast once the pressure lifts.
issue: "sleep" is both the cost and the cure in a two-sentence unit.

text: Strain gathered in your body during those years, and it showed first in your sleep. You pushed through on nerve, and you got through because a few people made you stop.
issue: "alone" clashes with "a few people" in the same sentence.

text: You ease into your body in these years, with better appetite and better sleep and more pleasure in ordinary days. You enjoy your health through this decade, and you feel at ease in your own skin.
issue: The line leans on the decade before, which the unit cannot see, and a helping decade can follow another helping one.

text: Support and good rest restore you in these ten years, and you recover quickly from strain. You sleep well and eat well, and your energy holds steady through the decade.
issue: The same lean on the decade before.

text: In you making and earning sit close together, and you are paid in the same season that you make.
issue: "the gap" has no referent after the Career line, so the reader cannot tell which gap.

text: Your energy has held steady since your late forties because you kept your sleep and your meals in order. You have more of it left than people who pushed hard and rested little.
issue: "kept" twice in two sentences.

text: Your progress at work since your late teens has come through what you studied, each qualification earned before you asked for the next step. At least once someone senior recommended you before you felt ready, and you have proved them right.
issue: On D082 the Sage stem beat beside it says "quietly put your name forward".

text: Unusual knowledge brings you work in these years, through research, advice or technical skill. You become the one people ask about what others do not know, and your name grows inside a small field.
issue: The last sentence turns on "People" and "your name", never on the reader.

text: Rivalry over shared work costs you energy in these years, and a joint effort takes more from you than it pays. You get through on work that is plainly yours, and the people who matter see that you did it.
issue: The last sentence ends on "the people who matter", not the reader.

text: Bosses have either backed you fully or tried to slow you down since your late teens, and few have stayed neutral about you. You have done your best work for the ones who believed in you, and you have outstayed most of the ones who did not.
issue: On D030 and D188 the lead above it says "you outlast most of the people who underrated you".

text: You do your best work inside an organisation with fixed rules and a visible ladder, and you climb it by doing every step properly. Because you need to know where you stand, open-ended jobs leave you uneasy, and a clear title settles you. What you gain is lasting rank, and what you lose is the freedom to move quickly.
issue: "proper" twice in one unit.

text: Routine tightens around your work in these years, and caution keeps you from moves that would pay more. Your reliability earns you respect, and you find a better fit once someone else sees what you are worth.
issue: "keeps" twice.

text: Ambition softens in these years, and the easy option keeps winning in your work. The value of what you make carries you on, and you move forward each time a deadline gives you a reason to finish.
issue: "keeps" twice.

text: You think best out loud, with one person close enough to hear the rough version and sharp enough to push back. Because your ideas only feel real once they have been tested on someone, an evening of silence at home leaves you restless. You give a partner your best ideas first, and your harshest opinions too.
issue: "Your partner" presumes the reader has one now. Q10 rules "a partner" at the Day Gate.

text: Your clearest thinking has happened alone, late at night or on long walks, away from the people you live with. More than once you have surprised a partner with a decision you had been weighing for weeks in silence.
issue: "So far" fits a reader inside the Day Gate. The same beat is shown to readers past 48 (here 67), for whom the gate (渊海子平: 日柱, the middle years and the partner) has closed.

text: Your clearest thinking has happened in long talks with someone close, more than in study or alone at a desk. You have changed your mind more than once because a partner disagreed, and you have also argued long after either of you was listening.
issue: The same "so far" slip, shown at 68.

text: You grow from your late forties by mastering one rare thing completely. You put what you learn into a form others can use, a method or a body of work, and you see it travel further than you do.
issue: The seat card beside it closes "your method stays unwritten for longer than it should".

text: Past your late forties you keep improving at what you already know, and each year adds polish more than novelty. You grow wiser through repetition and care, and you become the example others hold up.
issue: "A character" clashes with the house term for the ten (the characters), on a page that names them.

text: Since your late forties, people and daily life have held more of your thinking than ideas, and you have turned your curiosity to practical things.
issue: Without a comma it first reads "your late forties people".

text: Since your late forties you have found yourself explaining things you once took for granted, and it has taught you as much as it taught others. You have written down or passed on more of what you know than in all the years before.
issue: The time phrase attaches to "took for granted", so the sentence reads twice.

text: Your thinking sharpens against the ideas you are handed this year, and you find flaws in what others accept faster than you can keep them to yourself.
issue: "Received ideas" is C1 to C2 idiom.

text: You grow when life is hard, and you lose direction when it gets too comfortable. Because difficulty was where you first found your strength, you sign up for the harder option by choice, and a year with nothing hard in it leaves you restless. You have done your best learning in seasons other people would call their worst.
issue: On D043 this opener meets the owner-approved General year line, "You grow fastest this year where something forces you to". (D019, D128 and D191 have the same clash; D128 and D191 go with DD-014. D019's pair is two approved units, so it is the owner's call.)

text: You are the one who keeps a group working, the colleague who remembers the deadline and the friend who makes the plan happen. Because order calms you, you take on the organising without being asked, and people come to depend on it. Your place in a circle is quiet, and you decide more than anyone gives you credit for.
issue: Broken idiom (one credits a person with a thing, or gives credit for it).

text: Your friendships have grown out of work and shared duties since your late teens, the colleagues you trusted and the seniors who trusted you. Friends you had no shared task with drifted away, and you kept the ones bound to you by a duty for years after the job ended.
issue: A comparative with nothing to compare.

text: Comparison runs through your friendships in these years, and you notice who earns more and who wins more. What carries you is one friend who never competes with you, and you lean on that friend above all others.
issue: "often" is a banned hedge.

text: Friendship and contest mixed in those years, and more than once a friend took credit or a prize you had earned. The company itself got you through, and you learned to tell an ally from a competitor.
issue: Broken idiom.

text: When you were a child, your remarks were the ones repeated at family gatherings and in class. By your teens you had a few friends who loved your wit and a teacher or two who had given up on you.
issue: Dangling modifier ("As a child" attaches to "your remarks").

text: Other children took a while to warm to you, because you stood at the edge of each group for a long time before you joined it. By your teens you had one or two close friends who understood you, and they were enough for you.
issue: "as a child" repeats "Other children", and "for a long time first" is broken.

text: During those years you held yourself apart from most groups, sure that few people matched your standard. Your circle grew smaller than it had been, and you found the one or two friends who stayed were enough to carry you.
issue: The last sentence has the circle and the friends as its subjects, not the reader.

text: What was proper ruled your social life in those years, and you kept company with people you were expected to know. You were respected and a little lonely, and you found ease with one friend outside that circle.
issue: "Propriety" is above the B1–B2 band.

text: You widen your circle in these years, through travel and new groups and the people they lead you to. You make more new friends in this decade than in the one before it.
issue: "through … through" and "people … people" in one sentence.

text: Your circle widens this year through chance meetings and introductions, and you move easily between groups that never meet each other.
issue: Repeats "friends of friends" from the Horizon helping lived decade on D076, D115 and D183.

text: Competition runs through your circle this year for the same invitations and attention, and you share your friends more widely than you planned.
issue: "Competition … over" takes the wrong preposition (competition is for a thing). Its "runs through" frame also meets the Rival heavy decade's "Comparison runs through your friendships" on D076, D115 and D200, which DE-004's polish round takes, since a tweak keeps the opening.

text: Roles and expectations mark your friendships this year, a committee seat or a host's duty, and you are known for showing up when you said you would.
issue: Repeats the Magistrate heavy decade's "Duty shapes your friendships" on D011, D024, D029, D039, D099 and D127.

text: Friends meet you as peers this year, and you spend more time with people who do what you do than with those who look up to you.
issue: "equals" already carries the Twin's seat and decade lines on the same pages (five times on D145 and on D199).

text: The friends you made as a child were your equals, children who kept pace with you and stood up for you in turn. The friendships that lasted into your teens were the level ones, and you let the rest go without a fuss.
issue: Competition is the Rival's force, and on D024, D145 and D199 the Rival decade beside it says "friends who competed with you" (source: 渊海子平 论比肩, the Twin is the peer who stands level; 争夺 belongs to 劫财).

text: Those years filled your life with lively company, friends who competed with you and pushed you on. You were at your best among a crowd of rivals, and you won their respect openly.
issue: "equals" is the Twin's word in the Rival's decade (source: 三命通会 论比劫, 劫财 is the rival who takes a share).

text: Your circle widens from your mid-thirties through a partner's world, through their friends and their family and their work. You will meet the people who shape these years through someone you share a home with.
issue: The Day Gate spans 35 to 47, so twenty years runs into the Hour Gate, which holds its own seats (source: 三命通会 根苗花实, the Day pillar is the 花, the middle years).
